post.summary: Search Google Maps businesses by keyword and location

parameters.name: maxItems
parameters.description: optional row cap; pay-per-event actors that take the row count from their own input ignore it, so maxTotalChargeUsd is the spend limit

parameters.name: maxTotalChargeUsd
parameters.description: the spend cap Apify enforces on every event this run bills, in dollars. treg's key requires it, above 0 and at most 1, and holds it for the call

parameters.name: memory
parameters.description: MB of run memory. treg's key requires 1024, which fixes the actor-start charge; your own key may set any size

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: run timeout in seconds. treg's key requires 90 so the run and its rows arrive before any wait gives up; a larger pull should use your own key and the async web.scrape.job.* pair above

searchStringsArray.description: keywords to search, one per entry (dentist, plumber, coffee shop); each is searched inside locationQuery and every business becomes one row

locationQuery.description: where to search, as typed into Google Maps: 'Austin, TX', 'London, UK', or a whole country. Omit to let each term carry its own location

maxCrawledPlacesPerSearch.description: max businesses per search term, 1-500, counted AFTER filters; default 100

maxCrawledPlaces.description: total businesses across all terms; 0 = no ceiling. You pay per business returned, so set this to cap the bill

language.description: result language, e.g. en|es|fr|de|ja|zh-CN|vi; default en

scrapeContacts.description: look up each business site for emails and social links (emails, email_type, social_links). Default true — these fields are part of the result price, not an add-on

scrapePlaceDetailPage.description: also open each place's Maps page for hours, price_level, popular_times and any missing phone/site. Default false; makes a run noticeably longer

maxReviews.description: reviews to attach per business, 0-500; default 0 (none). A place page holds roughly the first 8

placeMinimumStars.description: keep only businesses rated at or above '1'|'2'|'3'|'4'|'4.5'; empty keeps all. Filtered-out places are not returned, not charged

website.description: allPlaces | withWebsite | withoutWebsite — filter on whether the business has its own site. Filtered-out places are not charged

skipClosedPlaces.description: leave out permanently-closed businesses so you do not pay for dead leads. Default true

geo_split.description: split a wide area into a grid and search each cell to get past Google's ~120-per-view ceiling. Default false; turn on for anything wider than a city

proxyUrls.description: leave empty to use the residential proxy included in the run price; or pass your own gateway URLs (http://user:pass@host:port)

post.description:
Performs a live HLR lookup, returning number type, live status, original and current network, and porting information. Warning: a national number sent without input_format can be read as another country's number (a US 617... number as an Australian 61... number), and that lookup is still charged.

Answers arrive in results[0]. live_status is LIVE, DEAD, ABSENT_SUBSCRIBER, NO_TELESERVICE_PROVISIONED, NOT_AVAILABLE_NETWORK_ONLY, NO_COVERAGE, INCONCLUSIVE or NOT_APPLICABLE; current_network_details names the serving network and is_ported says whether the number moved. Some networks give no live status (NOT_AVAILABLE_NETWORK_ONLY) but the lookup still costs a credit. Landlines and other non-mobile numbers return NO_COVERAGE and bad formats return BAD_FORMAT; both are free. A results[0].error other than NONE (INSUFFICIENT_CREDIT, TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, INTERNAL_ERROR, NULL_RESULT) is free and should be retried later.
